NFL DFS Quarterback Rankings: Week 12 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 29 · 9 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 28, 1:29 AM ET

Trevor Lawrence is the top-projected quarterback on the Week 12 DraftKings main slate at 21.8 DraftKings points for $6,700, against Tennessee. Joe Burrow (21.6, $7,700) and C.J. Stroud (20.5, $6,500) are next.

Mac Jones returns the most per dollar among quarterbacks projected for at least 15 points: 3.91 projected points per $1,000 at $4,000.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 28, 1:29 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Quarterbacks to know in Week 12

Trevor Lawrence, JAX vs TEN ($6,700)

Trevor Lawrence carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 21.8 DraftKings points at $6,700, the highest on the entire main slate. That is 0.1 points clear of Joe Burrow. The model includes 3.5 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 3.25 projected points per $1,000, 4th of 12 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Lawrence averaged 21.8 points with a simulated floor of 8.7 and a ceiling of 39.6, and he holds 21% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Jacksonville is a 14-point favorite at home against Tennessee, with an implied team total of 31.25 in a game totaled at 48.5.

Joe Burrow, CIN vs NO ($7,700)

Joe Burrow projects 2nd at the position with 21.6 DraftKings points at $7,700, 2nd on the main slate overall. The salary works out to 2.81 projected points per $1,000, 11th of 12 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Burrow averaged 21.6 points with a simulated floor of 8.6 and a ceiling of 39.3, and he holds 11% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Cincinnati is a 9.5-point favorite at home against New Orleans, with an implied team total of 29 in a game totaled at 48.5.

Value: Mac Jones, SF vs SEA ($4,000)

Mac Jones projects for 15.7 DraftKings points at $4,000, which works out to 3.91 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 12 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. Across 50,000 simulations Jones averaged 15.6 points with a simulated floor of 5.7 and a ceiling of 28.6, and he holds 5% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. San Francisco is a 1.5-point underdog at home against Seattle, with an implied team total of 20.5 in a game totaled at 42.5.
